member.name: T:BugSplatDotNet.BugSplat
member.summary:
Crash reporting for .NET and .NET Framework (4.7.2+) on Windows, built on the native BugSplat SDK (BugSplat.dll). Every report is a minidump that BugSplat symbolicates server-side from uploaded symbols, so managed frames get file names and line numbers without shipping PDBs.
* Crashes — installs the native unhandled-exception filter and WER handler. Unhandled managed exceptions and hard faults (access violations, fail-fast, stack overflow, corrupted heap, crashes inside P/Invoke) are captured as a minidump by BugSplatMonitor.exe. * Handled exceptions — , called from inside a catch, writes a minidump at the throw site without terminating the process.
BugSplat.dll, BugSplatMonitor.exe, BugSplatReporter.exe and BugSplatWer.dll must sit next to the application executable at run time, built for the architecture the process runs as. The BugSplat NuGet package ships x86, x64 and ARM64 and copies the matching set; the SDK download ships x64, so an app using it must run as a 64-bit process (a .NET Framework app needs PlatformTarget=x64: AnyCPU with Prefer32Bit runs as 32-bit).

member.name: P:BugSplatDotNet.BugSplat.IsWerEnabled
member.summary: True when BugSplat's WER runtime-exception helper (BugSplatWer.dll) is registered, i.e. crashes that bypass the in-process filter — fail-fasts, and crashes in packaged/WinUI 3 apps — will be captured. Registration requires an allowlist entry naming BugSplatWer.dll under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\Windows Error Reporting\RuntimeExceptionHelperModules (created with administrator rights). When this is false, those crashes are NOT reported; WinUI 3 apps in particular should surface a warning (see the MyDotNetWinUI3Crasher sample).

member.name: M:BugSplatDotNet.BugSplat.Post(System.Exception)
member.summary:
Reports a handled exception as a minidump and uploads it; the process keeps running. Call it from inside the catch block that caught : the dump is taken while the exception is being handled, so its throw-site frames are still on the stack and BugSplat shows them with file and line, like a crash. Called anywhere else there is no exception in flight and nothing is reported. Blocks while the report is written and, in quiet mode, uploaded. With the crash dialog it returns once the user has answered it, and the upload finishes in the background.
On 32-bit .NET Framework the runtime has already unwound the stack when a catch block runs, so the report shows where the exception was caught rather than where it was thrown. To keep the throw site there, call Post from an exception filter instead: catch (Exception ex) when (Report(ex)), with Report calling Post and returning true.
member.returns: True if the BugSplat monitor took the report.

member.name: M:BugSplatDotNet.BugSplat.PostFromCurrentContext
member.summary: Posts a dump of the calling thread as it stands, for when the runtime no longer has the exception's pointers: this thread's registers, described by an exception record carrying the CLR's exception code. The minidump is written from those structures while this method blocks, so they only have to live until it returns.

member.name: T:BugSplatDotNet.MiniDumpType
member.summary: Windows MINIDUMP_TYPE flags (declared in DbgHelp.h) that control how much process state a captured crash dump contains. Combine values with the bitwise-or operator.
member.remarks: Only the subset relevant to BugSplatDotNet is declared here. The full enumeration is at https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/api/minidumpapiset/ne-minidumpapiset-minidump_type.

member.name: F:BugSplatDotNet.MiniDumpType.Normal
member.summary: Thread stacks and the module list only — the smallest dump, and the default. Enough for BugSplat to name the managed frames with file and line.

member.name: F:BugSplatDotNet.MiniDumpType.WithDataSegs
member.summary: Include every module's writable data sections (global variables) — e.g. the CLR's live globals.

member.name: F:BugSplatDotNet.MiniDumpType.WithFullMemory
member.summary: Include all committed memory. Produces very large dumps; avoid for routine crash capture.

member.name: F:BugSplatDotNet.MiniDumpType.WithHandleData
member.summary: Include the process handle table.

member.name: F:BugSplatDotNet.MiniDumpType.WithUnloadedModules
member.summary: Include modules that were unloaded before the crash.

member.name: F:BugSplatDotNet.MiniDumpType.WithProcessThreadData
member.summary: Include thread environment (TEB/PEB) data.

member.name: F:BugSplatDotNet.MiniDumpType.WithPrivateReadWriteMemory
member.summary: Include private read-write committed memory, including the CLR's loader/JIT heaps and the GC heap. Dumps grow with the process's memory use (tens of MB and up), and BugSplatMonitor only writes them when full dumps are enabled for the application.

member.name: F:BugSplatDotNet.MiniDumpType.WithFullMemoryInfo
member.summary: Include virtual-memory region layout information (region bounds, not contents).

member.name: F:BugSplatDotNet.MiniDumpType.WithThreadInfo
member.summary: Include per-thread timing and start-address information.

member.name: F:BugSplatDotNet.MiniDumpType.IgnoreInaccessibleMemory
member.summary: Skip memory pages that cannot be read rather than failing the whole dump.

member.name: F:BugSplatDotNet.MiniDumpType.WithTokenInformation
member.summary: Include process/thread token (security) information.

member.name: F:BugSplatDotNet.MiniDumpType.WithModuleHeaders
member.summary: Include each module's PE headers.

member.name: F:BugSplatDotNet.MiniDumpType.FilterTriage
member.summary: Scrub the dump for triage (heapless, strips module paths/PII). Not recommended for managed analysis.
